topic.title: The ₹5 lakh reel is a rumour with a rate card
topic.claim: The big number for what a reel earns is mostly a story, and it works as marketing for the person quoted.
topic.behaviour: Articles and friends quote lakhs per reel. Young people start to feel a 15-second video is a salary, and brands feel they are getting a bargain or a prestige buy.
topic.mechanism: Rate figures are rarely checked, so a high number lifts the creator's price and makes the brand's spend look serious. Everyone in the room benefits from believing it.
topic.group: young people thinking of 'reels as a career', and marketers
topic.moment: A cousin says 'bhai, ek reel ke lakhs milte hain' and starts shooting in the balcony.

turn.believed: Top creators are paid lakhs per reel, so anyone can be.
turn.actually: The number is a quoted price nobody verifies, and it protects the price for the few who are actually booked.

topic.because: A high quoted price makes both creator and brand look important. Verifying it helps no one in the deal.

proof.fact: AajTak reports the top five Gen Z fashion influencers earn ₹2 lakh to ₹7 lakh per branded reel. The article says the rate figures are not attributed to the creators or verified.

topic.payoff: A price nobody can check is a story. Stories are what the page is actually selling.
topic.send_to: The sibling who just bought a ring light.
real_details: Brand endorsements are about 70% of earnings, and affiliate links add 5%-15% commission.
topic.news_peg: AajTak report on influencer rates per reel, 2026-10-27
topic.why_now: Festive-season brand budgets are about to be spent, and 'reels as a career' is trending again.

score.why: The lakhs-per-reel number is a quoted price nobody checks; matches his view on influencer marketing.
